smalldocs builds a website from a folder of Markdown pages and notebooks. A file `_smalldocs.yml` in
the folder holds the options of the site.

smalldocs looks like [Quarto](https://quarto.org), and reads its Markdown. Quarto is a tool that turns
Markdown and notebooks into websites, PDFs and slides. smalldocs also builds a Quarto project, from its
file `_quarto.yml`, with no change. It writes the site into the folder
`_site`. Each page of the site has a navbar at the top, a sidebar at the left and a table of contents
at the right. smalldocs also makes reference pages from your Python code, and pages that list other
pages, such as a blog.

The site can use any theme from [Bootswatch](https://bootswatch.com). A theme is a stylesheet that sets
the colours and the fonts of the site.

smalldocs is one Python package. It needs no Pandoc, no Deno, no Sass and no TeX. Install it from PyPI:

```bash
pip install smalldocs
```

Build a site, or preview it while you write:

```bash
smalldocs render docs      # writes docs/_site
smalldocs preview docs     # serves it at http://127.0.0.1:4200 and reloads on every change
```

## What smalldocs does not do

smalldocs makes websites only. It does not make PDF files, Word files, slides or books. It does not
run code. A notebook shows the outputs that were saved in it.

A project that uses only the website features of Quarto builds with Quarto or with smalldocs. The two
sites look alike. [From Quarto](guide/from-quarto.qmd) lists the differences, and the command
`smalldocs check` finds them in your project.
